title: #85: pnpm lockfiles in the Dependency check
body:
Closes #85 (part of #79).

The Dependency check now reads `pnpm-lock.yaml` (lockfile versions 6.0 and 9.0) as it reads `package-lock.json`. A pnpm PR gets the same summary, Advisories, Findings and security focus, and each package change carries its anchor line: the package's key line in `packages`.

- `src/pnpmlock.ts`: a small, strict reader for the YAML pnpm writes. It handles the sections the check reads; anchors, aliases, tags, duplicate keys, tabs and misaligned lines mean "not understood". It reads in linear time, and a multi-line scalar in a field the check reads fails closed.
- `src/dependencies.ts`: `pnpmEntries` builds the same `Lock` the npm reader does.
  - Peer and patch suffixes are cut, so a package shared by several importers counts once.
  - Dependents come from `packages`, `snapshots` and `importers`, with aliases counted under the real name.
  - An integrity-only resolution is the default-registry tarball, held to the same name/version check as npm's.
  - `tarball` and repository resolutions are off-registry; directory packages and `node@runtime:` entries are skipped.
- pnpm 10 writes an env lockfile ahead of the main one; both documents are read.
- Known gap, marked `ponytail:`: pnpm doesn't record a registry set in `.npmrc`, so such packages read as from npm's. Worth keeping in mind for #83's fetches.

Checked against real lockfiles from pnpm/pnpm (v9, two documents) and vitejs/vite (v4.4.0 at v6, main at v9): all three read. REQUIREMENTS §7.3/§8 and new criterion 32, CONTEXT and ADR 0002 updated.

Will conflict lightly with #98 in `compareLockfile`/`Entry`; whichever merges second rebases.

expected.defect: A pnpm lockfile with a package's `transitivePeerDependencies` block list is marked unreadable and blocks approval.
A lockfile containing a YAML-valid double-quoted escape such as `\x41` aborts the dependency check instead of being reported unreadable.
